title.narrative: Resilience and Sustainable Recovery of the Tombs of the Buganda Kings at Kasubi

description.narrative: The 24-month project will strengthen the long-term resilience, conservation, and sustainable management of the Tombs of the Buganda Kings at Kasubi by operationalizing integrated conservation, disaster risk reduction (DRR), tourism, and visitor management plans, improving buffer-zone protection, and upgrading interpretation spaces, signage, pathways, and accessibility features to enhance visitor experience and safeguard the site’s Outstanding Universal Value Implementation will include structured stakeholder consultations, technical collaboration with Japanese conservation and DRR experts, and institutional strengthening of governance mechanisms between the Buganda Kingdom and Ugandan authorities. The project will deliver targeted capacity-building programmes for women, youth, artisans, and site managers, fostering intergenerational transmission of skills and supporting the creation of heritage-based enterprises linked to sustainable tourism. Awareness campaigns and capacity building schemes will reinforce community ownership and cultural pride. At the regional level, the initiative will convene African heritage professionals to exchange lessons on post-disaster recovery and produce a best-practice report to support replication across the continent. Expected results include formally adopted and operational management frameworks, enhanced disaster preparedness, improved visitor experience, empowered communities benefiting from heritage-based livelihoods, and the positioning of Kasubi Tombs WHS as a model of resilient, community-centred heritage management in Africa.
